title: Livermore's nuclear-pumped space laser lens

>> Teller sat on my couch with me one afternoon.
tellings.difference: Adds that Teller showed him the lens while sitting on his couch at the Department of Energy, and names the program Excalibur.
tellings.link_reason: Harrington again tells of the Livermore nuclear-pumped space laser and its thumbnail-sized lens, here as shown to him by Teller.

as_told.title: Edward Teller shows Harrington the Excalibur lens

plain: In the 1980s, according to John S. Herrington, who was Secretary of Energy at the time, the Lawrence Livermore weapons laboratory worked on a space weapon that would set off a nuclear explosion in space and focus its energy through a lens "about the size of your thumbnail." Herrington tells Michels the physicist Edward Teller sat on his couch at the Department of Energy one afternoon and showed him the lens, and he names the programme Excalibur. He tells it as something he took part in himself.
